Accepted Papers

4 papers accepted for presentation at WLR 2026.

Towards Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Transformers

Jane Smith, Carlos Mendez, Wei Liu

Show abstract Hide abstract

We investigate the faithfulness of chain-of-thought reasoning traces produced by large language models and propose a suite of diagnostic tests that distinguish genuine multi-step inference from shortcut pattern matching. Our experiments on five reasoning benchmarks show that current models rely heavily on surface-level heuristics even when producing ostensibly correct reasoning chains.

Efficient In-Context Learning via Sparse Retrieval

Priya Nair, Tom Becker

Show abstract Hide abstract

We present SparseICL, a retrieval-augmented framework that selects a minimal yet maximally informative set of in-context exemplars. By combining BM25 pre-filtering with a learned reranker, SparseICL reduces prompt length by 60% while matching or exceeding full-retrieval baselines on twelve classification and generation tasks.

Calibration Under Distribution Shift with Temperature Ensembles

Anna Kowalski, Rajan Gupta, Mei Zhang, Oliver Brown

Show abstract Hide abstract

Deploying machine learning systems in the wild requires reliable uncertainty estimates even when test inputs differ from training data. We show that ensembles of temperature-scaled models substantially outperform single-model calibration approaches under covariate shift, and provide theoretical guarantees under a mild regularity condition on the shift magnitude.

Graph-Structured Memory for Long-Horizon Planning

Marcus Lehmann, Yuki Tanaka

Show abstract Hide abstract

We propose GraphMem, an external memory module that organises episodic experience as a typed knowledge graph, enabling agents to perform multi-hop lookup across thousands of past observations. On long-horizon tasks in BabyAI and Minecraft, GraphMem outperforms vanilla LSTM and Transformer baselines by 34 percentage points in task completion.
